# 1 Maccabees Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_011_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And the king of Egypt gathered a great army like the sand by the seashore and many ships, and he sought by treachery to gain Alexander's kingdom and add it to his own kingdom.

**2** And he went into Syria with peaceful words, and the people of the cities opened to him and met him, for Alexander the king had commanded them to meet him, because he was his father-in-law.

**3** But as Ptolemy entered the cities he stationed troops as a garrison in each city.

**4** And when he came near Azotus they showed him the temple of Dagon that had been burned and Azotus and its suburbs destroyed and the bodies cast about and those who had been burned whom Jonathan had burned in the war, for they had piled them up along his route.

**5** And they told the king what Jonathan had done, in order to blame him, but the king said nothing.

**6** And Jonathan met the king at Joppa with glory, and they greeted each other and slept there.

**7** And Jonathan went with the king as far as the river called Eleutherus and returned to Jerusalem.

**8** And Ptolemy the king gained possession of the cities along the seacoast as far as Seleucia-on-the-Sea, and he was devising evil plans against Alexander.

**9** And he sent ambassadors to Demetrius the king, saying: "Come, let us make a covenant one with the other, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander has, and you shall reign over your father's kingdom.

**10** For I have repented of having given him my daughter, for he sought to kill me."

**11** And he was false about him because he coveted his kingdom.

**12** And he took his daughter away from him and gave her to Demetrius, and Ptolemy estranged himself from Alexander, and their enmity was revealed.

**13** And Ptolemy entered Antioch and set on his head the crown of Asia; so he set two crowns upon his head, the crown of Egypt and the crown of Asia.

**14** And Alexander the king was in Cilicia at that time, because those in those parts were in revolt.

**15** And Alexander heard and came against him in war; and Ptolemy brought out his army and met him with a strong force and put him to flight.

**16** And Alexander fled into Arabia to find protection there, and Ptolemy the king was exalted.

**17** And Zabdiel the Arab cut off the head of Alexander and sent it to Ptolemy.

**18** And Ptolemy the king died three days later, and those in the fortresses were destroyed by those who were in the fortresses.

**19** And Demetrius became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.

**20** In those days Jonathan gathered those in Judea to attack the citadel that was in Jerusalem, and they built many engines of war against it.

**21** And certain lawless men who hated their own nation went to the king and reported to him that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.

**22** And the king was angry when he heard it, and immediately when he heard it he came to Ptolemais and wrote to Jonathan not to besiege it, and to come to him and meet him quickly.

**23** And Jonathan when he heard this commanded that they should continue the siege, and he chose some of the elders of Israel and some of the priests and put himself in danger.

**24** And he took silver and gold and garments and many other gifts and went to the king at Ptolemais, and he found favor in his sight.

**25** And though certain lawless men of his nation made complaints against him,

**26** the king treated him as his predecessors had treated him; he exalted him in the sight of all his friends,

**27** and he confirmed him in the high priesthood and all the other honors he had before, and gave him in gift the revenues of the first rank among the king's friends.

**28** And Jonathan petitioned the king and made him give Israel freedom from tribute and the three districts, and he promised him three hundred talents.

**29** And the king consented and wrote letters to Jonathan about all these things in these terms:

**30** "King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

**31** We send you the copy of the letter that we wrote to Lasthenes our kinsman about you, that you might know.

**32** King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.

**33** We have decided to do good to the nation of the Jews, who are our friends and observe what is just toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.

**34** We have confirmed to them the boundaries of Judea and the three districts of Aphaerema and Lydda and Ramathaim, which were added to Judea from Samaria, and all their appurtenances, to all those who sacrifice in Jerusalem, instead of the royal dues which the king received from them each year previously from the produce of the land and the fruit of the trees.

**35** And as for the other things that belonged to us from now on — the tithes and tolls that are due to us and the salt pits and the crown taxes — all these we grant to them as a release.

**36** And nothing of these shall be annulled from this time and forever.

**37** Now therefore take care to make a copy of these things, and let it be given to Jonathan and placed in the holy mountain in a conspicuous place."

**38** And Demetrius the king saw that the land was quiet before him and there was no resistance to him, and he sent away all his forces, each man to his own place, except for the foreign troops which he had recruited from the isles of the nations; so all the forces of his predecessors hated him.

**39** Now there was a man named Trypho who had been on Alexander's side; and he saw that all the army was murmuring against Demetrius; and he went to Imalkue the Arab who was rearing Antiochus the young son of Alexander,

**40** and he urged him and said to him: "Give me Antiochus that he may be king in his father's place." And he told him all that Demetrius had done and the hatred his forces had for him; and he stayed there many days.

**41** And Jonathan sent to Demetrius the king the request that he should remove the troops of the citadel from Jerusalem and the troops who were in the strongholds, for they kept fighting against Israel.

**42** And Demetrius sent to Jonathan, saying: "I will not only do this for you and your nation, but I will greatly honor you and your nation, when I find the opportunity.

**43** And now you will do right to send me men who will fight for me, for all my forces have revolted."

**44** And Jonathan sent him three thousand valiant men to Antioch; and they came to the king, and the king was glad at their coming.

**45** And those in the city gathered together — about one hundred and twenty thousand men — and they wanted to kill the king.

**46** And the king fled into the palace, and those in the city occupied the main streets of the city and began to fight.

**47** And the king called the Jews to his aid, and they all gathered to him at once and dispersed throughout the city, and they killed that day about one hundred thousand men.

**48** And they burned the city and took many spoils that day and saved the king.

**49** And those in the city saw that the Jews had gotten control of the city as they wished; and their spirit fell and they cried out to the king with supplications, saying:

**50** "Give us your right hand and let the Jews stop fighting against us and the city."

**51** And the king cast down his arms and made peace, and the Jews were honored in the sight of the king and in the sight of all those in his kingdom; and they returned to Jerusalem with great spoils.

**52** And Demetrius the king sat down on the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.

**53** But he lied about all that he had said, and estranged himself from Jonathan, and did not reward him according to the benefits he had shown him, but treated him very harshly.

**54** After this Trypho returned, and Antiochus the young child with him, and he reigned and put on the diadem.

**55** And there gathered to him all the forces which Demetrius had dismissed, and they fought against Demetrius, and he fled and was routed.

**56** And Trypho seized the elephants and took possession of Antioch.

**57** And the young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying: "I confirm to you the high priesthood and I appoint you over the four districts and that you be one of the king's friends."

**58** And he sent him golden vessels and a dinner service and gave him leave to drink in golden vessels and to be dressed in purple and to wear a golden brooch.

**59** And his brother Simon he appointed governor from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.

**60** And Jonathan went forth and traveled through the cities beyond the River, and all the forces of Syria gathered themselves to him as allies; and he came to Ashkelon and the men of the city met him honorably.

**61** And he went from there to Gaza, and the men of Gaza shut their gates against him; and he besieged it and burned its environs with fire and plundered them.

**62** And the men of Gaza petitioned Jonathan, and he gave them his right hand, and he took the sons of their rulers as hostages and sent them away to Jerusalem; and he passed through the country as far as Damascus.

**63** And Jonathan heard that the generals of Demetrius had come with a great army to Kedesh in Galilee, intending to remove him from the affairs of the country.

**64** And he went to meet them, and left his brother Simon in the country.

**65** And Simon encamped against Beth-zur and fought against it many days and shut them in.

**66** And they petitioned him to give them his right hand, and he gave it to them; but he expelled them from there and took possession of the city and set a garrison in it.

**67** And Jonathan and his army encamped at the water of Gennesareth, and early in the morning they journeyed to the plain of Hazor.

**68** And behold, the army of the foreigners met him in the plain; they had laid an ambush for him in the mountains, while they themselves came to meet him from the front.

**69** And those in ambush rose up out of their places and joined battle; and all those with Jonathan fled,

**70** not one was left of them except Mattathias the son of Absalom and Judas the son of Chalphi, commanders of the forces of the army.

**71** And Jonathan tore his clothes and put earth on his head and prayed.

**72** And Jonathan turned back to them to battle and routed them, and they fled.

**73** And those who were fleeing from him saw it and returned to him and pursued together with him to Kedesh to their camp and they encamped there.

**74** And there fell of the foreigners on that day about three thousand men; and Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
